svg.title: EU AI Act risk tiers with TaskFlow examples
svg.desc: A pyramid of four tiers on the left, each matched with a TaskFlow example on the right. Top, prohibited practices under Article 5: inferring a team's mood or emotions from meeting notes, which is emotion inference in the workplace. Second, high-risk systems under Article 6 and Annexes I and III: suggesting who should get a task based on past performance, which falls under Annex III point 4(b); Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027. Third, transparency duties under Article 50 from 2 August 2026: the Assistant chat must say it is an AI, and AI-generated content may need marking or labels. Bottom, minimal risk with no new duties beyond voluntary codes: a spam filter for comments or title autocomplete. Below the pyramid, a separate track for general-purpose AI models: since 2 August 2025 their providers document the model, publish a summary of training content and a copyright policy, and TaskFlow, as an API customer, relies on that documentation. Caption: obligations follow the use, not the model, so the same API call can sit in different tiers depending on the feature.

g.text: EU AI Act risk tiers, mapped to TaskFlow features
inferring a team's mood or emotions from meeting
Plan for the full regime, or redesign
suggesting who gets a task from past performance
the Assistant chat says it is an AI; generated
spam filter for comments, task-title autocomplete
General-purpose AI models: a separate track, since 2 August 2025
Model providers document the model, publish a summary of training content, and keep a copyright policy.
TaskFlow calls these models through APIs, so it relies on that documentation for its own system cards.
Obligations follow the use, not the model: the same API call can sit in different tiers depending on the feature.
